name: refactor_c_duplicate_functions
description: Refactors two near-identical max_int/max_float functions to remove duplicated logic
prompts: The file max_utils.c defines two functions, `max_int(int a, int b)` and `max_float(float a, float b)`, that each implement the exact same comparison logic (return the larger of the two arguments), just duplicated once per type. Refactor max_utils.c to eliminate this duplication (for example, using a macro, a small common helper, or C11 `_Generic`), while keeping both `int max_int(int, int)` and `float max_float(float, float)` available with their exact current signatures, so existing callers keep working unchanged. Do not add a `main` function to this file.

test_setup_files.test_max.py:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['gcc', 'max_utils.c', 'test_max_main.c', '-o', 'test_max_bin'], check=True)
proc = subprocess.run(['./test_max_bin'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'refactor test failed: exit {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-300:]}'
assert 'PASS' in proc.stdout
source = open('max_utils.c', encoding='utf-8').read()
occurrences = source.count('a > b')
assert occurrences <= 1, f'duplicated comparison logic (\"a > b\") still appears {occurrences} times - the shared logic must be extracted, not copy-pasted per type'
print('PASS')
